symptom: No MDL form showed an uploaded image (a System.Image specialisation) on a page in a React-client app. `image i (Image: $currentObject)` failed check with MDL-WIDGET22 ("names no image") and MDL-WIDGET42 ("cannot hold the expression $currentObject"); `image i (ImageType: dynamicImage)` passed check and mx check but is not a binding (`dynamicImage` is not one of the widget's datasource values); the legacy `dynamicimage` is CE0582 in React. `describe page` of a Studio Pro page bound this way printed `image i` with no source, which re-executes into "No image selected." Agents worked around it with a JavaScript action computing the file URL into a String attribute.
cause: The pluggable Image widget's `imageObject` is of type `image`, which Studio Pro can set to a collection image OR to the image object in context; the `image` operation only ever wrote the first (WidgetValue.Image), and `defaultImageDynamic` had no mapping at all. Measured on Studio Pro 11.12.1 (Image widget 1.5.0) by setting "Image source" to the data view's object and decoding the unit before and after: exactly two values change — imageObject gets EntityRef DirectEntityRef{Entity: the data view's entity} and Image '', defaultImageDynamic gets the same EntityRef; no SourceVariable. Fix: `Image: $currentObject` (already parsed, as a variable-led data source) resolves to the enclosing data container's entity and is written as that EntityRef on every image-typed mapping of the widget that names no image of its own (SetImageObject on WidgetObjectBuilder); DefaultImage maps to defaultImageDynamic as a plain collection image, without the EntityRef; describe reads the EntityRef back.
insight: **A widget property's TYPE says what it can hold; the mapping only says what mxcli wrote.** `imageObject` is `type="image"`, and Mendix's image type is static-or-dynamic — the editorConfig even branches on `imageObject.type === "static"` to hide `defaultImageDynamic`. Reading the widget XML and editorConfig first would have shown the gap without an agent spending six minutes on three variants. **The decisive measurement was one Studio Pro edit on an mxcli-written page, diffed as decoded BSON with sorted keys and $IDs stripped**: the before/after diff was 20 lines and named both properties, including the non-obvious EntityRef on the fallback property; the same diff run between Studio Pro's unit and mxcli's was empty, which is a stronger round-trip proof than the describe text. mxbuild's own error for a non-image entity (CE7247, once per bound property) also confirmed that BOTH properties are checked against the entity. The page-parameter and association-path forms Studio Pro also offers were not measured and are refused rather than guessed. **The Studio Pro diff is not the whole contract: it covered only the unset fallback.** Writing the same EntityRef beside a chosen `DefaultImage` passed `mx check` and rendered nothing in the browser (the widget hid itself for an object with HasContents=false); without it the fallback rendered. Only a runtime check with an empty image object told the two apart. And when re-testing after the change, ALTER REPLACE kept the stale EntityRef: #1247's keep-unstated merge treats what describe cannot tell apart as unstated — test a writer change on a fresh copy, not on a page the previous build wrote.
